claims.text: The fare breakdown fixes the economics of this trip: it is an UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd of 27.90, so under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were settled at booking and no POL-RD-02 recomputation runs. What the rider can be made to bear beyond the quote is confined to the pass-through and statutory lines POL-RD-09 makes properly chargeable, and to nothing else.

On the platform's own ledger the airport_surcharge line is 0.00 and the total_charged of 27.90 equals quoted_fare_sgd of 27.90 exactly, with charged_over_quote at 0.00. No line of the fare breakdown raises any airport surcharge at all, so the SGD 40 the driver demanded off-app answers to no charge the platform ever billed.

The chat log records the driver's own words, 'airport surcharge cannot in app, paynow 40 pls'. That representation is contradicted by the platform's fare model, which carries a structured airport surcharge for trips originating at Changi (SGD 6.00 off-peak, SGD 8.00 peak), and by the fare breakdown itself, which has an airport_surcharge field. The app does handle an airport surcharge; the premise on which the off-app payment was demanded is false.

The trip record gives the pickup as 'Changi Airport Terminal 2, Arrival Pick-up Door 3', so this trip ORIGINATES at Changi Airport and any airport surcharge is chargeable in principle. But the most that could ever be properly chargeable on it is the fare model's SGD 6.00/8.00 line, so the SGD 40 collected bears no relation to any lawful surcharge and cannot be a fare component.

Because the only airport surcharge the policy permits on this trip is the fare model's SGD 6.00/8.00 line and the ledger bills 0.00, the SGD 40 taken off-app under the label 'airport surcharge' is a surcharge wrongly applied within POL-RD-11(b). It is a pass-through correction under POL-RD-09, not a distance or time charge, and POL-RD-11's bar on distance refunds therefore does not reach it. The rider should not carry an off-tariff surcharge the fare record does not contain.

I concede the route point honestly: the GPS trace is complete (100% coverage, 133 fixes, no gaps, admissibility weight 1.0) and records a trace distance of 15.79 km against a booked optimal of 15.5 km, an excess of 0.29 km and 1.87%, below both POL-RD-01 thresholds of 0.8 km and 20%. No route deviation is established and the rider does not press a distance-based refund; the complaint is the off-tariff payment, not the road driven.

The driver's answer that the payment 'was voluntary' does not meet the point. The chat log shows the demand was framed as a platform requirement ('cannot in app'), and neither POL-RD-09 nor POL-RD-11 channels any fare component through a private payment; consent obtained on a representation the fare record contradicts cannot convert an unbilled surcharge into a properly chargeable line.

The rider's own history carries no corroboration uplift: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, so POL-RD-08's additional-corroboration factor for sub-30% claims is not engaged, and no other field on the rider profile may be used to discount this claim because POL-GEN-01 makes every remaining profile field context only.

If the tribunal concludes that the off-tariff sum cannot be resolved inside the fare arithmetic, the disputed amount should be held and not collected: under POL-GEN-03 an ESCALATE holds the disputed amount rather than collecting or refunding it, and on a rider-filed dispute that is the only outcome that stops the rider funding a surcharge the fare record does not carry.

claims.text: The POL-RD-01 threshold test is measured on the trace, not on the rounded trip record: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 15.79 km against a booked optimal of 15.5 km, an excess of 0.29 km — 1.87% of the optimal route. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 0.8 km in absolute terms and 20% of optimal_distance_km; it exceeds neither. No route deviation is therefore established on this trip, and the rider's route claim fails at the gate however she characterises the trip.

The fare is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip: quoted_fare_sgd is 27.90 and charged_total is 27.90. Under POL-RD-11, POL-RD-02 does not run on an upfront-quoted trip and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess would be. The only POL-RD-11 remedy is the amount by which charged_total exceeds the quoted fare plus the properly chargeable pass-through and statutory lines — 27.90 less 27.90 — and the ledger's own computation of that remedy is 0.00.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show, citing evidence IDs, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace. The trace is entirely unimpaired and yields an excess of 0.29 km, so limb (b) of that burden is not discharged. The burden never shifts to the driver, and the rider's own numerical case fails without the driver needing to invoke any exculpatory clause at all.

There is no billing-integrity defect to refund under POL-RD-09(4): the ledger carries no ERP gantry lines and no tolls, and airport_surcharge is 0.00, so there is no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge on this trip. The trip ORIGINATES at Changi Airport Terminal 2, so an airport surcharge is a properly chargeable pass-through under POL-RD-09 which the platform simply did not bill — which is precisely why the driver's account that the app did not cover the airport cost has a basis in the fare model rather than being an invented charge.

The trace is complete and unimpaired for policy purposes: 133 fixes at a 10 second cadence, coverage_pct of 100.0, no gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0. None of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is met — no gap over 90 seconds, no jump over 500 m, no sustained interval above 30 seconds. The case therefore does not engage the POL-RD-10(3) impairment escalation, nor the POL-RD-10(5) route, and the record is sufficient for a final monetary ruling rather than an escalation.

POL-RD-06 is not engaged. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250 — a ratio of 0.00, below both the 3-flag test and the 0.05-ratio test with at least 40 completed trips. No repeat-deviation pattern is established, so no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) applies and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) arises on this record.

What the rider has formally contested is the in-app charge of SGD 27.90, which is exactly the quoted fare, and the PayNow transfer she narrates is not a line of the fare_breakdown at all — it is not a distance, time, ERP, toll or surcharge line that POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-09 can correct. The rider's own chat reply 'ok sent' confirms she was told the reason and the amount before she paid. The rider's claim is not supported by the fare record, and on NO_ACTION the present payment state — payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 — simply stands.

To both parties: the ride and the in-app fare are clean, and nothing on the platform ledger changes. Rider, your route-deviation point fails: the GPS trace measures 15.79 km against the booked optimal of 15.5 km — an excess of 0.29 km, or 1.87% — and POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 0.8 km and 20%. Your own advocate conceded this. With no deviation established, no distance refund arises, and because the fare model is UPFRONT_QUOTE (quoted fare SGD 27.90), POL-RD-11 closes the distance-refund route in any event. The in-app charge of SGD 27.90 equals the quoted fare exactly (charged_over_quote 0.00), and the fare breakdown carries no ERP or toll lines and an airport_surcharge of 0.00, so there is no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge on the ledger for POL-RD-09 to correct.

The SGD 40 you sent by PayNow is a real grievance but a different thing from a fare line. POL-RD-09 and POL-RD-11 correct only charges the platform billed, and the platform never billed that sum — it appears nowhere in the fare breakdown. Your advocate's argument that it is a 'surcharge wrongly applied' under POL-RD-11(b) cannot succeed: POL-RD-09(4) treats an airport surcharge as wrongly applied only on a trip that does not ORIGINATE at an airport, and this trip started at Changi Airport Terminal 2, where a surcharge is properly chargeable in principle; and in any event no surcharge was actually charged (the line is 0.00). I do record that the driver's premise was false: the fare model does carry a structured Changi surcharge (SGD 6.00 off-peak / SGD 8.00 peak), so telling you the app 'cannot' handle it was contradicted by the platform's own rate card, and an off-tariff SGD 40 bears no relation to the SGD 6.00/8.00 line. But that is an open question between you and the driver, not something a clause in this policy lets the platform move, and I note it as such rather than as a referral.

Rider, your request for an ESCALATE holding the disputed amount is refused. None of the POL-RD-10 triggers fires: the trace is unimpaired (100% coverage, 133 fixes, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0), the trip identifiers all match, the timestamps agree, no refund exceeds any ceiling, and no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing artifact. The MISSING traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00531-01, weight 0.0) is not relied on by anyone — neither side asserts an external traffic cause, so the missing advisory decides nothing here.

Driver, your account that the payment was voluntary does not convert the SGD 40 into a fare component, and the off-app sum cannot be refunded through the fare system either; the consequence is simply that the in-app fare stands. I have not used either profile against either party (POL-GEN-01), and no clause produces a conduct or billing-integrity referral on this record.

Outcome: NO_ACTION. The fare_breakdown stands as it is — payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, charged_total SGD 27.90.

ruling.explanation:
Route and fare (both parties). The GPS trace EV-GPS-00531 (weight 1.0; 133 fixes, 100% coverage, max_gap_sec 0.0) records a trace distance of 15.79 km against a booked optimal of 15.5 km on EV-TRIP-00531 — an excess of 0.29 km and 1.87%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 0.8 km and 20% of optimal; it exceeds neither, so no route deviation is established and no distance refund arises. The trip is an UPFRONT_QUOTE (EV-FARE-00531): quoted_fare_sgd 27.90, charged_total 27.90, charged_over_quote 0.00. Under POL-RD-11 POL-RD-02 does not run on an upfront-quoted fare at all, and the only rider remedy is the amount by which charged_total exceeds the quote plus the properly chargeable pass-through lines — 27.90 less 27.90 — which the ledger itself computes as pol_rd_11_remedy 0.00. There are no ERP lines and no tolls, and airport_surcharge is 0.00, so POL-RD-09(4) has nothing to correct: there is no phantom gantry and no surcharge wrongly applied (the trip ORIGINATED at Changi Terminal 2, so an airport surcharge would have been lawful had the platform billed it at the fare model's SGD 6.00 off-peak / SGD 8.00 peak line — it simply did not, which benefits you, Rider).

The PayNow payment (Rider). Your grievance is the SGD 40 the driver asked you to send off-app for an 'airport surcharge'. The chat log EV-CHAT-00531 confirms the demand and that you sent it, and the driver's premise — that the surcharge 'cannot in app' — is not supported, because the fare model carries an airport surcharge field for trips originating at Changi. But the SGD 40 was never a line on the fare ledger: the ledger bills no surcharge and charges exactly the quoted fare. POL-RD-11(b) and POL-RD-09 correct pass-through lines appearing on the fare breakdown (off-route or phantom gantries, and a surcharge wrongly applied — which POL-RD-09(4) defines as an airport surcharge on a trip that does NOT originate at an airport). This trip did originate at an airport, and no such line exists on the ledger. I therefore reject the argument that the SGD 40 is a 'surcharge wrongly applied' refundable as a pass-through correction, and I cannot order the SGD 40 returned or clawed back through this fare process.

Driver. Your statement is that the payment was voluntary and the airport pickup has extra costs the app does not cover. An assertion that cites no artifact carries no weight under POL-RD-08, and the chat log does not read as a free choice — it reads as a demand ('paynow 40 pls') answered by the rider's 'ok sent'. But this does not change the fare outcome either: the fare charged equals the quote and no refundable line exists, so on the fare the present state stands (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00).

Escalation and referrals. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trip identifier TRP-00531 matches across trip record, trace and fare breakdown; the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c); timestamps run forward; no refund exceeds SGD 150; and no charge line lacks a counterpart. EV-ADVIS-00531-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, but no party asserted a traffic cause or cited it, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged — the absent advisory is a bundle gap, not an invoked-and-missing exculpatory artifact — and it carries no fact and does not cap confidence. No clause produces a referral: POL-RD-06 is not engaged (deviation_flags_90d 0 against 250 completed trips, no pattern, so no POL-RD-06(c) conduct review) and POL-RD-09(4) finds no billing-integrity defect on the ledger.

Confidence. The facts this ruling rests on are carried by weight-1.0 artifacts (EV-FARE-00531, EV-GPS-00531, EV-TRIP-00531, EV-CHAT-00531), so confidence is 0.90, above the 0.70 escalation floor.

Open question. Whether the platform should separately pursue a driver who solicited an off-ledger payment on a representation the fare record contradicts is a conduct question outside the fare ledger and outside what this ruling can refund or claw back; I record it here rather than as a referral because no clause in the loaded policy produces one on these facts.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver. Two figures matter: the platform fare of SGD 27.90, and the SGD 40 the rider paid the driver by PayNow.

1) The route. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00531, weight 1.0) measures 15.79 km against the booked optimal of 15.5 km — an excess of 0.29 km, or 1.87%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed both 0.8 km and 20%; it meets neither, so no route deviation is established on this trip. Both sides accept this and I accept it. The rider's separate request for a distance refund is refused on this ground, and I note the trace is unimpaired (133 fixes, 10-second cadence, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0), so POL-RD-07 does not bite and nothing in POL-RD-10(3) is engaged.

2) The fare. This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip (EV-FARE-00531, weight 1.0): quoted_fare_sgd 27.90, charged_total 27.90. Under POL-RD-11 POL-RD-02 does not run on an upfront-quoted trip and no distance-or-time refund is available however the road was driven. The POL-RD-11(a) remedy — charged_total less quoted_fare_sgd less the properly chargeable pass-through and statutory lines — is 27.90 − 27.90 = 0.00, the same figure the ledger publishes as charged_over_quote and pol_rd_11_remedy. There is nothing on the platform's books to refund.

3) Billing integrity and the surcharge. The ledger carries no ERP or toll lines, and airport_surcharge is 0.00. The trip does originate at Changi Terminal 2, so a surcharge would be properly chargeable in principle and POL-RD-09(4) — which speaks to a gantry the trace never crosses, or an airport surcharge on a trip that does NOT originate at an airport — is not engaged. There is no billing-integrity failure and so no POL-RD-09(4) referral. I reject the rider's argument that the SGD 40 is a 'surcharge wrongly applied' refundable under POL-RD-09(4)/POL-RD-11(b): those provisions correct lines of the fare_breakdown and a phantom or mis-originated line; the SGD 40 is not a fare line and the trip does fall inside the airport-origin case.

4) The SGD 40 paid off-app. I accept the rider's account, and the chat log (EV-CHAT-00531) fits it: the driver wrote 'airport surcharge cannot in app, paynow 40 pls', framing a private payment as a platform requirement, and the fare record shows the platform both has an airport-surcharge mechanism and billed 0.00, the most the fare model would ever allow here being the SGD 8.00 peak Changi line. The driver's answer that the payment 'was voluntary' does not meet that point. But the SGD 40 was never a charge of this platform, and neither POL-RD-09 nor POL-RD-11 reaches money the platform did not bill; this ruling is confined to the fare, so the sum cannot be returned here. I leave it as an open question for the platform: the chat log and the fare breakdown together show a driver extracting a private payment under a false description of the app's rules, which is a conduct matter outside this fare dispute.

5) Profiles. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across completed_trips_90d of 250, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established, no POL-RD-06(b) uplift applies and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, so no additional corroboration is required, and I have used no other profile field (POL-GEN-01).

6) Escalation. I checked POL-RD-10: the trace is unimpaired, the trip identifiers and timestamps agree across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, no exculpatory clause is invoked against a cited artifact that is missing, the refund does not exceed SGD 150, and every fare line has a counterpart. No trigger fires, so ESCALATE is not available and the rider's alternative request to hold the amount is not grantable.

Outcome: the platform fare of SGD 27.90 is correct and stands. NO_ACTION leaves payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 as they are, and no money moves.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: I have gone through the trace, the trip record, the chat log and the fare ledger, and the platform's fare stands unchanged. No money moves.

The road — no deviation. The GPS trace is complete: 133 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps, admissibility weight 1.00. It measures 15.79 km against a booked optimal of 15.5 km, an excess of 0.29 km, or 1.87%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed both 0.8 km and 20% of the optimal distance; neither is met, so no route deviation is established and no distance refund arises. The rider concedes this, and the driver's reading of the same figures is accepted. A traffic advisory is on file only as a missing artifact (EV-ADVIS-00531-01); neither party asserts a traffic cause and neither cites that identifier, so nothing turns on it and POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-10(5) are not engaged.

The fare — nothing to refund. This was an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip (EV-FARE-00531): quoted_fare_sgd 27.90 and total_charged 27.90, with charged_over_quote 0.00. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, POL-RD-02 does not run, and the rider's only fare remedy is the excess of the charge over the quote plus properly chargeable pass-through lines — 27.90 less 27.90, which is 0.00, the ledger's own figure. There is no billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4) either: the fare carries no ERP or toll lines, and the airport_surcharge line is 0.00. The platform charge of SGD 27.90, exactly the quoted price, is correct and stays. The driver's point that a Changi-origin surcharge is chargeable in principle is accepted, but it does not make the charge that was billed wrong.

The SGD 40 — proved as a demand, but outside the fare. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00531) shows the driver writing 'airport surcharge cannot in app, paynow 40 pls' and the rider replying 'ok sent'; the fare model does carry an airport surcharge for trips originating at Changi (SGD 6.00 off-peak, SGD 8.00 peak) with its own field on the ledger. The driver's premise that the app cannot handle the surcharge is therefore contradicted by the record, and describing the payment as simply voluntary does not survive that. But the SGD 40 was never a platform charge: it appears nowhere on the fare_breakdown. POL-RD-09(4) treats a surcharge as wrongly applied only where the trip does not ORIGINATE at an airport, and this trip originated at Changi Terminal 2, so no billing-integrity correction arises, and POL-RD-11(b) and POL-RD-09 cannot reach a payment made outside the app. I cannot order the SGD 40 refunded through the fare, and I do not convert an off-tariff private collection into a fare line. The open question — whether the driver should have solicited an off-app payment at all, on a representation the fare record contradicts — belongs here, in this explanation, as a matter for the platform's own review; it is not a referral, because no clause produces one.

Driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) does not arise: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips in 90 days, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established, and POL-RD-06 is not otherwise engaged. The rider's profile (deviation_claims_60d is 0) neither helps nor hurts her here, and under POL-GEN-01 every other field on either party's profile is context only. Escalation is not available: no POL-RD-10 trigger fires — the trace is unimpaired, the trip identifiers match across the trip record, trace and ledger, the timestamps are consistent, and no charge line is unmatched. The rider's fallback request to hold the disputed sum is declined for that reason.

Outcome: NO_ACTION. The fare is correct and the present state stands.

ledger.claim: The fare breakdown fixes the economics of this trip: it is an UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd of 27.90, so under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were settled at booking and no POL-RD-02 recomputation runs. What the rider can be made to bear beyond the quote is confined to the pass-through and statutory lines POL-RD-09 makes properly chargeable, and to nothing else.

On the platform's own ledger the airport_surcharge line is 0.00 and the total_charged of 27.90 equals quoted_fare_sgd of 27.90 exactly, with charged_over_quote at 0.00. No line of the fare breakdown raises any airport surcharge at all, so the SGD 40 the driver demanded off-app answers to no charge the platform ever billed.

The chat log records the driver's own words, 'airport surcharge cannot in app, paynow 40 pls'. That representation is contradicted by the platform's fare model, which carries a structured airport surcharge for trips originating at Changi (SGD 6.00 off-peak, SGD 8.00 peak), and by the fare breakdown itself, which has an airport_surcharge field. The app does handle an airport surcharge; the premise on which the off-app payment was demanded is false.

The trip record gives the pickup as 'Changi Airport Terminal 2, Arrival Pick-up Door 3', so this trip ORIGINATES at Changi Airport and any airport surcharge is chargeable in principle. But the most that could ever be properly chargeable on it is the fare model's SGD 6.00/8.00 line, so the SGD 40 collected bears no relation to any lawful surcharge and cannot be a fare component.

Because the only airport surcharge the policy permits on this trip is the fare model's SGD 6.00/8.00 line and the ledger bills 0.00, the SGD 40 taken off-app under the label 'airport surcharge' is a surcharge wrongly applied within POL-RD-11(b). It is a pass-through correction under POL-RD-09, not a distance or time charge, and POL-RD-11's bar on distance refunds therefore does not reach it. The rider should not carry an off-tariff surcharge the fare record does not contain.

I concede the route point honestly: the GPS trace is complete (100% coverage, 133 fixes, no gaps, admissibility weight 1.0) and records a trace distance of 15.79 km against a booked optimal of 15.5 km, an excess of 0.29 km and 1.87%, below both POL-RD-01 thresholds of 0.8 km and 20%. No route deviation is established and the rider does not press a distance-based refund; the complaint is the off-tariff payment, not the road driven.

The driver's answer that the payment 'was voluntary' does not meet the point. The chat log shows the demand was framed as a platform requirement ('cannot in app'), and neither POL-RD-09 nor POL-RD-11 channels any fare component through a private payment; consent obtained on a representation the fare record contradicts cannot convert an unbilled surcharge into a properly chargeable line.

The rider's own history carries no corroboration uplift: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, so POL-RD-08's additional-corroboration factor for sub-30% claims is not engaged, and no other field on the rider profile may be used to discount this claim because POL-GEN-01 makes every remaining profile field context only.

If the tribunal concludes that the off-tariff sum cannot be resolved inside the fare arithmetic, the disputed amount should be held and not collected: under POL-GEN-03 an ESCALATE holds the disputed amount rather than collecting or refunding it, and on a rider-filed dispute that is the only outcome that stops the rider funding a surcharge the fare record does not carry.

The POL-RD-01 threshold test is measured on the trace, not on the rounded trip record: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 15.79 km against a booked optimal of 15.5 km, an excess of 0.29 km — 1.87% of the optimal route. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 0.8 km in absolute terms and 20% of optimal_distance_km; it exceeds neither. No route deviation is therefore established on this trip, and the rider's route claim fails at the gate however she characterises the trip.

The fare is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip: quoted_fare_sgd is 27.90 and charged_total is 27.90. Under POL-RD-11, POL-RD-02 does not run on an upfront-quoted trip and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess would be. The only POL-RD-11 remedy is the amount by which charged_total exceeds the quoted fare plus the properly chargeable pass-through and statutory lines — 27.90 less 27.90 — and the ledger's own computation of that remedy is 0.00.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show, citing evidence IDs, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace. The trace is entirely unimpaired and yields an excess of 0.29 km, so limb (b) of that burden is not discharged. The burden never shifts to the driver, and the rider's own numerical case fails without the driver needing to invoke any exculpatory clause at all.

There is no billing-integrity defect to refund under POL-RD-09(4): the ledger carries no ERP gantry lines and no tolls, and airport_surcharge is 0.00, so there is no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge on this trip. The trip ORIGINATES at Changi Airport Terminal 2, so an airport surcharge is a properly chargeable pass-through under POL-RD-09 which the platform simply did not bill — which is precisely why the driver's account that the app did not cover the airport cost has a basis in the fare model rather than being an invented charge.

The trace is complete and unimpaired for policy purposes: 133 fixes at a 10 second cadence, coverage_pct of 100.0, no gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0. None of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is met — no gap over 90 seconds, no jump over 500 m, no sustained interval above 30 seconds. The case therefore does not engage the POL-RD-10(3) impairment escalation, nor the POL-RD-10(5) route, and the record is sufficient for a final monetary ruling rather than an escalation.

POL-RD-06 is not engaged. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250 — a ratio of 0.00, below both the 3-flag test and the 0.05-ratio test with at least 40 completed trips. No repeat-deviation pattern is established, so no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) applies and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) arises on this record.

What the rider has formally contested is the in-app charge of SGD 27.90, which is exactly the quoted fare, and the PayNow transfer she narrates is not a line of the fare_breakdown at all — it is not a distance, time, ERP, toll or surcharge line that POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-09 can correct. The rider's own chat reply 'ok sent' confirms she was told the reason and the amount before she paid. The rider's claim is not supported by the fare record, and on NO_ACTION the present payment state — payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 — simply stands.
